completed_passage:
Our town had a short fun run on Friday evening. My sister and I went to watch. The runners had numbers pinned to the fronts of their shirts, on their chests. We could read them as they came towards us. I wanted to see number 24. That was my father.

At first, there were many people beside the road. We could not see over their heads, so we stood on a small hill. From there, we had a clear view of the runners. A woman said the first runners would arrive soon. We waited and looked for number 24.

Soon the sky became dark. The numbers were hard to read, because the lamps along this part of the road were off. My sister took a small light out of her bag. She did not shine it into anyone's eyes. She pointed it down at a card we were holding. The card said, “Go, Dad!”

A runner waved when he saw our card. It was Dad. Several other runners passed him as we watched. He was moving more slowly than those runners, but he was smiling. We shouted his name. At the finish, he thanked us for the card.

“Did you win?” I asked. “No,” he said, “but last time I stopped twice. Today I ran all the way without stopping.” He was happy about that. My sister and I gave him some water because he was thirsty. Then we walked home together, carrying the little light and our card.
